text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed higher on reports of cold weather in Brazil. A significant polar air-mass might pass the coffee areas from the evening of July 5 which could present the greatest frost threat seen so far this year, Brazil's meteorologists Somar said on Monday. But in fresh comments on Tuesday, the agency said a larger polar air-mass could break into smaller masses, thus reducing the possibility of a damaging cold this weekend. Following yesterday's report of a downward revision in USDA's estimate for Indonesia the department informed us that the production figure for 1997/98 (April/March) has remained unchanged at 6.8 million bags, down from 7.6 million bags estimated for 1996/97. July added $35 to close at $1,800 per tonne, while September closed $25 higher at $1,822 per tonne.

In New York arabica futures closed higher although with pared gains. July added 4.10 cents/lb to close at 196.50 cents/lb, while September closed 2.85 cents/lb higher at 175.25 cents/lb. The gains were attributed to frost concerns in Brazil for the weekend, although most weather services contend the cold air will remain south of the coffee areas. Reports of a port strike in Santos, Brazil, aided sentiment. But the build up in stocks certified for delivery against the exchange, as well as an increase in stocks pending certification, could weigh on prices on Wednesday.
UNITED STATES - The CSCE reported certified coffee stocks rose by 1,783 60-kg bags as of June 30, to 49,900 bags. There were 27,313 bags pending grading, the exchange said.

ANGOLA - According to official sources coffee production in 1997/98 (April/March) is likely to reach 100,000 bags, up from an estimated 86,000 bags produced in 1996/97. Angola's coffee industry, like many of its other sectors, is struggling to recover from two decades of civil war between the government and former rebel UNITA movement. A 1994 peace treaty has bolstered agricultural output, although a serious lack of funding and millions of land mines scattered throughout the countryside continues to hamper production, a Reuters report said.

CANADA - Canada imported 232,299 bags of coffee in March 1997, 1.6 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1997 up to 736,100 bags, roughly 12 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1996. Total imports in calendar year 1996 rose by 9 per cent to 2.739 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in January/March 1997 were Guatemala (84,900 vs 73,000 bags), Brazil (73,600 vs 32,700 bags) and Colombia (104,900 vs 124,000 bags).
The country exported 124,900 bags of coffee in January/March 1997, 87 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1996. Total exports in calendar year 1996 rose by 18 per cent to 357,800 bags.
